newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends higher, buoyed by soy.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends higher, buoyed by soy.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures ended higher on spillover strength from CBOT soy contracts, and the May contract gained relative to the March as players rolled out their long positions, traders said.
"There was liquidation of long positions in the March ahead of first notice date (on Feb 28)," a trader said.
Another trader said the March/May spread fluctuated wildly Thursday, trading at 20-1/2 cents earlier, but narrowing late to settle at under 18 cents.
U.S. wheat markets drew support from CBOT soybeans and soymeal, which rose on buying by funds and commercials.
One trader said a key feature in Minneapolis was the July spring wheat contract's loss relative to KCBT July.
"A lot of people have been buying MGE July, selling KCBT July recently," another trader said. "People who are in that spread will lose money tonight."
Traders said the relative weakness in MGE July wheat amid forecasts of large spring wheat reserves at the end of the current crop marketing year.
"There's so much spring wheat in on-farm storage, and it's going to have to go somewhere," a trader said.
MGE spring wheat settled 2-3/4 cents to six cents per bushel higher, with March up 2-3/4 cents at $3.94-1/4. May gained five cents to settle at $3.76.
Brokerage LFG was a featured player, selling 1.2 million May bushels early but buying back 1.4 million May late.
